primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Barth syndrome due to TAFAZZIN (TAZ) deficiency
mechanism: TAFAZZIN encodes tafazzin, an inner-mitochondrial-membrane phospholipid transacylase required for remodeling immature cardiolipin into mature cardiolipin species. Defective cardiolipin remodeling disrupts mitochondrial membrane organization and respiratory-chain function, producing the X-linked Barth syndrome phenotype.
vignette: A 5-month-old boy has dilated cardiomyopathy, neutropenia, poor growth, and proximal muscle weakness. Urine testing shows increased 3-methylglutaconic acid. His maternal uncle died in infancy of heart failure. Genetic testing identifies a pathogenic variant in TAFAZZIN.
lead: The affected protein normally performs which of the following functions?
correct: Remodeling cardiolipin in the inner mitochondrial membrane
distractors: Transporting long-chain fatty acids into mitochondria through the carnitine shuttle
Oxidizing very-long-chain fatty acids in peroxisomes
Transferring electrons from complex I to coenzyme Q
distractor_notes: The carnitine shuttle uses CPT1, carnitine-acylcarnitine translocase, and CPT2; tafazzin instead remodels cardiolipin.
Peroxisomal very-long-chain fatty-acid metabolism is unrelated to tafazzin's phospholipid-remodeling function.
Complex I contains many subunits and transfers electrons to ubiquinone, but tafazzin is not a respiratory-chain electron carrier.
Mitochondrial DNA polymerase gamma, not tafazzin, performs mtDNA replication.
key_expl: Barth syndrome is an X-linked disorder caused by TAFAZZIN variants. Tafazzin is a phospholipid transacylase that remodels cardiolipin in the inner mitochondrial membrane. Abnormal cardiolipin impairs mitochondrial membrane and respiratory-chain organization, producing cardiomyopathy, neutropenia, skeletal myopathy, growth delay, and 3-methylglutaconic aciduria.
objective: Identify defective mitochondrial cardiolipin remodeling by tafazzin as the molecular defect in Barth syndrome.
